岡.meaning: A tiny goat with stubby <part>horns</part> wants a <part>mountain</part> of his own, so the farmer builds a <part>frame</part> of planks, lays <part>one</part> board across the top and piles turf over it. The goat climbs it every morning and bleats like a king. It's only a little <kanji>mount</kanji>, but it's his.
岡.on: From the top he licks an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne that the farmer holds up.
岡.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' gasps a <sound>ca</sound>rp, peeping out of the pond at the goat on his hill.

綱.meaning: A spider on one <part>ridge</part> wants to visit her friend on the next. She spins <part>thread</part> after thread and braids them until the line is as thick as an arm, then ties it round a boulder. Ships could moor to it now. Her bridge is a <kanji>hawser</kanji>.
綱.on: Her friend sends an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne sliding across it on a hook.
綱.kun: Halfway over she sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and drops her <sound>na</sound>an into the valley.

鋼.meaning: Two knights duel on a windy mountain <part>ridge</part>. One swings a gleaming <part>gold</part> sword, the other a plain grey one. Clang! The gold blade bends like a banana, and the grey one doesn't even chip. The gold knight squints at the plain blade and sighs: <kanji>steel</kanji>.
鋼.on: The winner treats the loser to a soft ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne.
鋼.kun: Back home, the smith hammers the grey blade's twin into a <sound>ha</sound>rp, a <sound>ga</sound>rlic press and hooks for a fishing <sound>ne</sound>t.

沸.meaning: A miser opens his water bill in the bath, sees the <part>dollar sign</part> and turns red. He's so cross that the <part>water drops</part> on his skin begin to bubble, and the tub steams like a kettle. He doesn't shout. He just sits there and starts to <kanji>seethe</kanji>.
沸.on: He sticks one bare <sound>foot</sound> out of the tub, pink as a lobster.
沸.kun: His rubber duck cries '<sound>Wah</sound>!' and leaps out onto the mat.

潤.meaning: A sulky <part>king</part> stands behind his palace <part>gate</part> in a heatwave, refusing to let the rain in. The clouds just squeeze through the bars, and <part>water drops</part> soak his crown, his beard and his royal socks. No gate can stop him getting <kanji>wet</kanji>.
潤.on: He hides under a <sound>jun</sound>iper bush, but it drips on him too.
潤.kun: The cook brings him hot <sound>u</sound>don, a kanga<sound>roo</sound> splashes in the puddles, and the queen says, '<sound>Oh</sound>, lovely.'

括.meaning: A sailor has lost his rope, so his pet chameleon wraps its long sticky <part>tongue</part> round the <part>anchor</part> and the dock post and holds on all night. By morning the boat hasn't drifted an inch. A lizard's tongue is the best way to <kanji>fasten</kanji> a boat.
括.on: As a reward, the sailor fries him a crispy <sound>katsu</sound> cutlet.
括.kun: A <sound>cuckoo</sound> on the mast watches the whole night, very impressed.

江.meaning: A carpenter's <part>workbench</part> floats off in a storm and wedges itself between two rocks. <part>Water drops</part> pile up behind it, ducks move in, and soon there's a little side stream with a diving board. Now the carpenter goes fishing in his own <kanji>creek</kanji>.
江.on: He sells the ducks an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne each from his bench.
江.kun: One duck lays an <sound>e</sound>gg on the diving board.

堀.meaning: A mole digs a trench round her vegetable patch to keep the rabbits out. The hard <part>soil</part> won't <part>yield</part>, so she bends double, scratching and sulking, until at last it gives way. The rabbits simply hop over. Still, she's proud of her <kanji>ditch</kanji>.
堀.on: After the rain, a black <sound>coot</sound> paddles up and down it.
堀.kun: She eats a <sound>ho</sound>tdog on its <sound>ree</sound>dy bank and admires the view.

泡.meaning: A fish wants to mail some sea to her cousin in a goldfish bowl. She tries to <part>pack up</part> the <part>water drops</part> one at a time, wrapping each in a thin skin of air, and posts the lot. When the cousin opens the parcel, all she gets is <kanji>bubbles</kanji>.
泡.on: The postman keeps the parcel wet with a garden <sound>ho</sound>se all the way.
泡.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' says the cousin, and dips each one in <sound>wa</sound>sabi before it pops.

叔.meaning: Every family party, the same guest arrives late, holding a dusty <part>candlestick</part> to light his way and a giant salty <part>pretzel</part> as a gift. He tells the same pirate story, eats all the crisps and naps on the sofa. Everyone loves him. He's your <kanji>uncle</kanji>.
叔.on: He always has a <sound>su</sound>gar <sound>cu</sound>be in his pocket for the children.

冒.meaning: A stubborn owl bets a crow she can keep one <part>eye</part> open through the whole noon <part>sun</part>. She perches on the church roof, squinting, feathers steaming, while the crows place bets. She wins, but sees spots for a week. Owls shouldn't take that <kanji>risk</kanji>.
冒.on: She sleeps it off in the cool shade of a big <sound>bou</sound>lder.
冒.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' cries a <sound>ca</sound>rp in the pond, who wants to dare it next.

俗.meaning: In a quiet <part>valley</part>, a fancy hotel has one gold <part>coat hook</part> by its door. A loud tourist hangs his dripping swimsuit on it, eats soup with his fingers and yodels at the cows. The butler faints. Such manners are <kanji>vulgar</kanji>.
俗.on: The cows yodel back, and so do <sound>Zo</sound>e from the flower stall and her pet <sound>cu</sound>ckoo.

佐.meaning: A famous magician has a nervous <part>coat hook</part> that stands at his <part>left</part> in every show, holding his cape, his wand and a rabbit. When a trick goes wrong, the hook quietly waves the rabbit. The crowd claps for the magician, but the real star is his <kanji>assistant</kanji>.
佐.on: After the show, the hook is paid with one <sound>sa</sound>rdine.

網.meaning: A spider in an old churchyard is tired of losing flies, so she knits thick <part>thread</part> into a proper fishing <part>net</part> and hangs it from a mossy <part>tombstone</part>. Next morning it holds three flies, a kite and a very surprised owl. She wins first prize for <kanji>netting</kanji>.
網.on: The groundskeeper's lawn <sound>mow</sound>er gets tangled in it too.
網.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' squeaks a <sound>mee</sound>rkat, caught in one corner.

陥.meaning: A tired fort from <part>old times</part> still flies one faded <part>pennant</part>. A boy throws a <part>boomerang</part> that clips the flagpole on its way back. The pole wobbles, the walls sigh, and the whole fort folds up like a deckchair. One tap was all it needed to <kanji>collapse</kanji>.
陥.on: The boy lays a pink <sound>car</sound>nation on the rubble to say sorry.
陥.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>,' groans a mouse, as its <sound>chee</sound>se falls into a crack.

弦.meaning: An archer's string snaps the night before the contest. Her granny pulls a <part>spool</part> of silver thread from her knitting bag and strings the <part>bow</part> while humming. Next morning every arrow plays a note as it flies. Granny's thread makes a singing <kanji>bowstring</kanji>.
弦.on: Her friend <sound>Gen</sound>, the hiker, hums along with every note.
弦.kun: When she sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', the string twangs and a <sound>roo</sound>k flaps off the target.

枠.meaning: A lost hiker finds a <part>signpost</part> in the woods pointing at a <part>tree</part>. She sees nothing special, then steps back: the post's arm and two branches make a perfect square around a view of the lake. Someone has built the forest a picture <kanji>frame</kanji>.
枠.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' she gasps, and a <sound>coo</sound>k from the cabin runs out to see.

倫.meaning: A robot works in the town <part>library</part> and hangs its rulebook on a <part>coat hook</part> by the desk: don't eat the books, return what you borrow, never shush a crying baby. It reads the list every morning. Nobody programmed it to be good; it chose these <kanji>ethics</kanji>.
倫.on: When someone finds a lost gold <sound>rin</sound>g, the robot hangs it on the hook until the owner comes back.

奉.meaning: Every spring, a <part>large</part> farmer stands on the hill with his arms spread wide, holding up a <part>pole</part> hung with <part>two</part> ribbons, while the whole village bows to the clouds and sings for rain. Nobody remembers why, but they never skip it. It's their oldest <kanji>observance</kanji>.
奉.on: If the clouds don't answer, his wife sprays everyone with a garden <sound>ho</sound>se.
奉.kun: Then they offer the sky a <sound>ta</sound>co, a <sound>te</sound>nt and a jar of <sound>ma</sound>ma's jam, and the farmer sneezes: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'

袖.meaning: A farmer's rusty <part>weathervane</part> is stuck, so he ties the arm of an old shirt to it as a windsock. The <part>reason</part> it works: the empty cuff fills with wind and points the way it blows. Now the farm's best weather forecaster is a <kanji>sleeve</kanji>.
袖.on: He hangs an old <sound>shoe</sound> on the vane's other arm to balance it.
袖.kun: The cat on the <sound>so</sound>fa bats at the flapping cuff through the window until she topples off the <sound>de</sound>sk.

猟.meaning: On the first day of the season, a hunter crouches behind a <part>fence</part> with a <part>fishhook</part> on a stick. A cheeky deer sets off <part>fireworks</part> right behind him. He leaps over the fence, his hat lands on the deer's antlers, and the deer strolls off wearing it. So much for <kanji>game-hunting</kanji>.
猟.on: He spends the rest of the trip sulking at a cosy <sound>ryo</sound>kan.
猟.kun: For dinner the innkeeper serves him <sound>ca</sound>rp and a plate of <sound>ree</sound>f fish.

狩.meaning: A museum <part>guard</part> has lost the night key, so he ties a <part>fishhook</part> to a string and dangles it through every air vent, crack and statue's ear in the building. At 3 a.m. it snags something: the key, and a very old sandwich. It was a long <kanji>hunt</kanji>.
狩.on: He celebrates with a cup of tea and four lumps of <sound>su</sound>gar.
狩.kun: From the last vent he also fishes out a toy <sound>ca</sound>rp.

妊.meaning: A <part>woman</part> starts spinning wool on her grandmother's <part>spindle</part>, and every week the socks she knits get smaller: grown-up size, child size, then little ones no bigger than a thumb. Her friends see the pile of booties and grin. Nine months of knitting: a <kanji>pregnancy</kanji>.
妊.on: A <sound>nin</sound>ja quietly leaves extra wool on her doorstep every night.
妊.kun: Her husband plays the <sound>ha</sound>rp to the bump, and her friends cheer, '<sound>Rah</sound>-rah!'

缶.meaning: A magician claims he can fit a whole <part>mountain</part> into a <part>bucket</part>. He waves his wand, there's a loud clang, and the bucket shrinks into a shiny little cylinder with a ring pull. Open it up: snow, a goat and pine trees. A mountain in a <kanji>tin can</kanji>.
缶.on: He tops each one with a pink <sound>car</sound>nation and sells them at the fair.
缶.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>rp buys one as a present for his <sound>ma</sound>ma.

鈍.meaning: A cowboy ties his horse to the <part>hitching post</part> and sits down to lunch with his brand-new <part>gold</part> knife. He saws at his steak. He saws at the butter. Nothing gets cut. The horse eats his lunch while he's still sawing. Pretty, but <kanji>dull</kanji>.
鈍.on: His <sound>don</sound>key happily licks the butter off the useless blade.
鈍.kun: A <sound>nee</sound>dle is sharper, and so is a <sound>bu</sound>ll's horn.

漂.meaning: After a vote on a ferry, one <part>ballot</part> blows overboard. It rides the <part>water drops</part> for weeks, past whales and islands, and washes up on a beach where a crab counts it. The crab wins, one vote to none. That's how far a ballot can <kanji>drift</kanji>.
漂.on: A lady in high <sound>hee</sound>ls, spinning a <sound>yo</sound>-yo, hands the crab its winner's sash.
漂.kun: The crab bows, '<sound>Ta</sound>-<sound>da</sound>!', and celebrates with a pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt.

苗.meaning: In a <part>rice field</part>, the frogs run a nursery. Each one babysits a tiny green shoot poking up like <part>grass</part>, sings it lullabies and shades it with a leaf umbrella. In summer they'll hand it back to the farmer, all grown. For now, every frog has a <kanji>seedling</kanji>.
苗.on: One frog ties his to a sli<sound>my</sound> <sound>yo</sound>-yo so it can't wander off.
苗.kun: Another feeds his crumbs of <sound>na</sound>an and a drop of <sound>e</sound>gg yolk.

巣.meaning: A family of sparrows can't find twigs, so they move into a bowl of <part>fruit</part> on a kitchen windowsill, with grapes for pillows and a banana for a roof. When <part>fireworks</part> burst over town one summer night, three chicks peek out from between the pears. Best <kanji>nest</kanji> in town.
巣.on: Mum bathes the chicks with a sliver of <sound>soa</sound>p from the sink.
巣.kun: The plate of <sound>su</sound>shi beside the bowl becomes their balcony.

僧.meaning: By the monastery door hangs one <part>coat hook</part> holding a sparkly leather jacket. It belongs to the gentle man in orange robes who sweeps the yard: <part>formerly</part> a rock star, now he only hums. Nobody would guess the drummer inside the quiet <kanji>monk</kanji>.
僧.on: He still washes with a bar of <sound>soa</sound>p carved like a guitar.

恒.meaning: A diner's oldest customer, a tortoise, orders the same <part>burger</part> at noon every day for ninety years. The cook could set a clock by him, and her <part>heartbeat</part> keeps time with his slow chewing. Storms, wars, new menus: nothing changes him. That's <kanji>constancy</kanji>.
恒.on: For pudding, every single day, one vanilla ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne.
恒.kun: And every day he sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and the cook catches it in her hair<sound>ne</sound>t.
